title: Maximum Sum of an Hourglass
description:
You are given an m x n integer matrix grid . 
 
 We define an hourglass as a part of the matrix with the following form: 
 [Figure: https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2022/08/21/img.jpg] 
 
 Return the maximum sum of the elements of an hourglass . 
 
 Note that an hourglass cannot be rotated and must be entirely contained within the matrix. 

 Example 1: 
 [Figure: https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2022/08/21/1.jpg] 
 
```
Input:
 grid = [[6,2,1,3],[4,2,1,5],[9,2,8,7],[4,1,2,9]]

Output:
 30

Explanation:
 The cells shown above represent the hourglass with the maximum sum: 6 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 9 + 2 + 8 = 30.
```

 Example 2: 
 [Figure: https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2022/08/21/2.jpg] 
 
```
Input:
 grid = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]

Output:
 35

Explanation:
 There is only one hourglass in the matrix, with the sum: 1 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 9 = 35.
```

 Constraints: 

 m == grid.length 
 
 n == grid[i].length 
 
 3 <= m, n <= 150 
 
 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 6
code: class Solution {public:int maxSum(vector<vector<int>>& grid){int m=grid.size(),n=grid[0].size(),best=0;for(int i=0;i+2<m;i++)for(int j=0;j+2<n;j++){int s=grid[i][j]+grid[i][j+1]+grid[i][j+2]+grid[i+1][j+1]+grid[i+2][j]+grid[i+2][j+1]+grid[i+2][j+2];best=max(best,s);}return best;}};
approach_summary: Turn repeated range sums or range updates into constant-time arithmetic.
